common_rust.name: Common Rust
symptoms: Small reddish-brown to rust-colored pustules may appear on both sides of maize leaves.
Pustules can become more numerous as disease develops.
Severely affected leaves may show yellowing or reduced photosynthetic area.
favorable_conditions: Cool to moderate temperatures can favor disease development.
Extended periods of leaf wetness can support infection.
prevention: Use locally recommended resistant or tolerant varieties where available.
Monitor fields regularly for early symptoms.
management: Scout regularly and identify symptoms early.
Follow current agricultural extension recommendations before applying any fungicide.
common_rust.source: Agricultural extension and crop-disease reference material; local recommendations should be verified before treatment.

gray_leaf_spot.name: Gray Leaf Spot
symptoms: Lesions may begin as small pale or tan spots.
Lesions can develop into elongated rectangular or gray-brown areas.
Multiple lesions may merge and reduce the functional leaf area.
favorable_conditions: Warm and humid conditions can favor disease development.
Extended periods of leaf wetness can increase disease risk.
prevention: Use suitable resistant or tolerant varieties where available.
Remove or manage infected crop residues according to local recommendations.
Maintain appropriate field management and monitor crop development.
management: Scout lower leaves and monitor disease progression.
Use locally recommended integrated disease-management practices.
Consult agricultural extension guidance before selecting chemical treatment.
gray_leaf_spot.source: Agricultural extension and crop-disease reference material; local recommendations should be verified before treatment.

healthy.name: Healthy
symptoms: No strong visual evidence of the four target diseases was detected.
prevention: Maintain appropriate irrigation, nutrition, sanitation, and field management.
Monitor newly developing leaves for changes.
management: No disease-specific treatment should be recommended solely from this classification.

northern_leaf_blight.name: Northern Leaf Blight
symptoms: Long, elongated gray-green to tan lesions may develop on maize leaves.
Lesions can expand and become more visible as disease progresses.
Severe infection can reduce healthy leaf area.
favorable_conditions: Moderate temperatures and prolonged leaf wetness can favor disease development.
Humid conditions can increase disease risk.
prevention: Use suitable resistant or tolerant varieties where available.
Manage infected crop residue according to local agricultural recommendations.
Scout fields regularly for early symptoms.
management: Monitor disease progression across the crop.
Use integrated disease-management practices recommended for the local region.
Consult current agricultural extension recommendations before applying fungicides.
northern_leaf_blight.source: Agricultural extension and crop-disease reference material; local recommendations should be verified before treatment.
